plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and large, rose-like blooms. Hundreds of cultivars exist, with single, semi-double, and fully double flower forms. It thrives in mild, humid climates with acidic soil and partial shade.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring, peaking in winter
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Western Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the plant that produces all true tea. Camellia japonica was celebrated in Japan for centuries as a symbol of the samurai because the whole flower drops intact.

plants.name: Delosperma cooperi
plants.description: A mat-forming succulent groundcover with daisy-like flowers that open in sunlight. In Southern Hemisphere summer it produces vivid blooms over fleshy, drought-tolerant foliage.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer (December to March), with a long season
plants.location: Native to the Eastern Cape and Free State of South Africa; grown in rock gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The flower petals are actually modified, and the glistening look of the leaves comes from bladder-like cells that store water, giving the plant its 'ice plant' name.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low-growing perennial with nodding, cup-shaped white flowers with golden stamens and leathery evergreen leaves. It blooms in the cold of winter, often pushing through snow in woodland gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe; cultivated in temperate gardens of Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite the name, it is not a rose at all but a member of the buttercup family, and all parts of it are poisonous. Folklore says it first bloomed from the tears of a girl who had no gift for the Christ child.

plants.name: Metrosideros excelsa
plants.description: A coastal evergreen tree covered in brilliant crimson, brush-like flowers made up of masses of long stamens. It often clings to sea cliffs and can form huge, spreading, gnarled canopies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer (late November to January)
plants.location: Native to the North Island coasts of New Zealand; planted in Australia, California, and South Africa
plants.funFact: Its flowering coincides with Christmas in New Zealand, and it is a cultural treasure (taonga) to the Māori. Some specimens are hundreds of years old.
